extracted.intended_audience: spectrum licensees, spectrum lessees, satellite operators, and applicants using FCC Form 608 / ICFS
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards for entering into, filing, and operating spectrum leasing (including short-term de facto transfer, spectrum manager leasing, SCS, private commons) and for electronic filing of international/satellite applications in ICFS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory FCC Form 608 & prior consent for short-term de facto transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties entering into a short-term de facto transfer leasing arrangement are required to file an electronic application with the Commission, using FCC Form 608, and obtain Commission consent prior to consummating the transfer of de facto control of the leased spectrum, except that parties falling within § 1.913(d) may file either electronically or manually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must be filed and Commission consent obtained before consummation. Exception for § 1.913(d) allows manual filing for some parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and required certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: To be accepted for filing under immediate approval procedures, the application must be sufficiently complete and contain all information and certifications requested on FCC Form 608, including information/certifications relating to the spectrum lessee's eligibility, basic qualifications, and foreign ownership required by rules of this chapter and service-specific rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete filings will not be accepted. Include all form fields and any service-specific required certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of required application fee (treated as transfer of control)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must include payment of the required application fee; for purposes of determining the applicable application fee, the application will be treated as a transfer of control (see § 1.1102).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate applicable fee using transfer-of-control rules; payment must accompany filing (see later ICFS payment steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: No waiver or declaratory ruling required for eligibility under immediate procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum leasing arrangement must not require a waiver of, or declaratory ruling, pertaining to any applicable Commission rules to qualify for immediate approval procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the arrangement needs a waiver or declaratory ruling, it cannot use the immediate approval path and must follow alternate procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: ULS reflection of consent and effective processing timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is filed electronically, consent will be reflected in ULS on the next business day after filing; if filed manually, consent will be reflected in ULS on the next business day after the necessary data from the manually filed application is entered into ULS. Consent is not deemed granted until the Bureau affirmatively acts upon the application, as reflected in ULS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume consent until ULS shows affirmative action. Timing differs for electronic vs manual filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and reconsideration of grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant of consent under these procedures will be reflected in a public notice (see § 1.933(a)) promptly issued after grant, and is subject to reconsideration (see §§ 1.106(f), 1.108, 1.113).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-grant public notice is issued; grants can be reconsidered under standard Commission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of leasing arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum leasing arrangement will be deemed effective in the Commission's records on the date set forth in the application. If the Commission consents after that specified date, the spectrum leasing application will become effective on the date of the Commission affirmative consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective date in Commission records is either the date in the application (if consent timely) or the date of affirmative consent; plan operations accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year limit on short-term de facto transfer use of expedited procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee and spectrum lessee may not use the special rules and expedited procedures for arrangements that in fact will exceed one year, or that the parties reasonably expect to exceed one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the arrangement will or is expected to exceed one year, use long-term procedures instead of short-term expedited rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file appropriate long-term application before expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee and spectrum lessee must submit, in sufficient time prior to expiration of the short-term arrangement, the appropriate application under the rules and procedures applicable to long-term de facto leasing arrangements, and obtain Commission consent pursuant to those procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing is required to avoid lapse; parties should plan transition filings well before expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration date and return of leased spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: A short-term spectrum leasing arrangement will expire on the termination date set forth in the arrangement; Commission approval includes consent to return the leased spectrum to the licensee at the end of the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End-of-term reversion to licensee is automatic under the approval; ensure termination date is clearly specified in the arrangement and application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions limited to total one-year for short-term arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: A short-term arrangement may be extended beyond the initial term provided that the initial term and extension(s) together would not result in a leasing arrangement that exceeds a total of one year (upon proper application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are allowed but total aggregate term cannot exceed one year for short-term classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of early termination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a spectrum leasing arrangement is terminated earlier than the termination date, the licensee must file a notification with the Commission no later than ten (10) days after the early termination, indicating the date of termination. If the parties fail to put the arrangement into effect, they must notify the Commission consistent with these provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File timely termination notices (10-day deadline) to the Commission to maintain accurate records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to long-term: compliance and unjust enrichment payment
rubrics_metrics.description: To convert a short-term arrangement into a long-term de facto transfer leasing arrangement beyond the one-year limit, parties may do so only if they comply with long-term procedures and, if the licensee is subject to transfer restrictions/unjust enrichment provisions, pay any unjust enrichment that would have been owed had the licensee filed a long-term application at the time of the initial short-term application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion requires retroactive compliance including potential unjust enrichment payments for protected licensees (see § 1.2110 and § 24.709).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion prohibited when long-term would have been barred
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are not permitted to convert a short-term arrangement into a long-term arrangement if the parties would have been restricted from entering into a long-term arrangement in the first instance because of a transfer, use, or other restriction applicable to the particular service (see § 1.9030).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must determine at the outset whether long-term arrangements would have been permissible; prohibited circumstances cannot be cured by conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment, transfer of control, and revocation rules mirror long-term provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules applicable to long-term de facto transfer leasing arrangements for assignment (§ 1.9030(g)), transfer of control (§ 1.9030(h)), and revocation/automatic cancellation (§ 1.9030(i)) apply in the same manner to short-term de facto transfer leasing arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat short-term arrangements as subject to the same assignment, transfer-of-control, and revocation regimes as long-term for these specific rule aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: No subleasing by short-term de facto transfer lessee
rubrics_metrics.description: A spectrum lessee that has entered into a short-term de facto transfer leasing arrangement is not permitted to enter into a spectrum subleasing arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subleasing is explicitly prohibited for lessees under short-term de facto transfer arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal constraints for short-term arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The renewal rules applicable to long-term arrangements apply to short-term arrangements, except that renewal of a short-term arrangement that would extend into the term of the renewed license cannot enable the combined terms of the short-term arrangements to exceed one year. The Commission must be notified of the renewal at the same time the licensee submits its application for license renewal (see § 1.949).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewals cannot be used to circumvent the one-year aggregate limit; notify Commission concurrently with license renewal filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community notification for certain Contraband Interdiction Systems (CIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten days prior to deploying a CIS that prevents communications to or from mobile devices, a lessee must notify the community in which the correctional facility is located. Notification must include description of system purpose, scheduled start date, and location, and be tailored to reach the community immediately adjacent (local TV, radio, Internet news, community groups). No notification required for brief tests prior to deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted local media and community outlets; allow at least 10 days prior notice; brief tests are exempted from notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract provision — lessee compliance and potential revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must state that the spectrum lessee must comply at all times with applicable rules and law, and that the spectrum leasing arrangement may be revoked, cancelled, or terminated by the licensee or Commission if the lessee fails to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit compliance and enforcement language in leasing contracts to reflect regulatory expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract provision — no continuing authority if license revoked
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must state that if the license is revoked, cancelled, terminated, or otherwise ceases to be in effect, the spectrum lessee has no continuing authority or right to use the leased spectrum unless otherwise authorized by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract should acknowledge forfeiture of lessee authority upon license termination and require lessee to cease operations absent Commission authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract provision — arrangement is not assignment/sale of license
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must state that the spectrum leasing arrangement is not an assignment, sale, or transfer of the license itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify in agreement that leasing confers usage rights only, not ownership of the license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract provision — restriction on assigning to ineligible entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must state that the spectrum leasing arrangement shall not be assigned to any entity that is ineligible or unqualified to enter into a spectrum leasing arrangement under the applicable rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include representations/warranties and assignment restrictions to ensure compliance with eligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract provision — consent for assignments must comply with Commission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must state that the licensee shall not consent to an assignment of a spectrum leasing arrangement unless such assignment complies with applicable Commission rules and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require that any assignment be conditioned on compliance with FCC assignment processes and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional contractual provisions for licensees under installment payment program
rubrics_metrics.description: If licensee holds licenses subject to the Commission's installment payment program, agreements must include an express acknowledgement that the license remains subject to the Commission's priority lien and security interest, and that the lessee shall not hold itself out to the public as the holder of the license or as a licensee by virtue of the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include lien/security-interest acknowledgement and public-facing limitations to prevent misrepresentation of licensee status.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBRS spectrum manager leasing scope (Priority Access Licensees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to § 96.32, a Priority Access Licensee may engage in spectrum manager leasing for any portion of its spectrum or geographic area, outside of the PAL Protection Area, for any bandwidth or duration within the terms of the license with any entity that has provided a certification to the Commission or pursuant to general notification procedures of § 1.9020(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure operations are outside PAL Protection Area and within license terms; certification or notification required.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBRS lessee certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The lessee seeking to engage in spectrum manager leasing must certify with the Commission that it meets the same eligibility and qualification requirements applicable to the licensee before entering into a spectrum manager leasing arrangement and must maintain accuracy of such certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority Access Licensees are deemed to meet certification; others may certify via ULS/FCC Form 608. Maintain ongoing accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBRS notification content to SAS Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to lessee operation, the licensee must submit notification to the Spectrum Access System (SAS) Administrator by electronic filing including lessee contact information, lessee FRN, name of real party in interest and FRN, specific spectrum leased (bandwidth and geographic area including call signs), and duration of the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete lessee identification and precise spectrum/time parameters in the SAS notification before operation commences.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBRS extension and termination notification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A spectrum leasing arrangement may be extended beyond the initial term for an additional period not to exceed the term of the Priority Access License, provided the licensee notifies the SAS Administrator in advance; early termination requires notification to SAS no later than ten (10) days after termination; failure to put into effect must be reported promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow SAS notification timing rules for extensions and early terminations; keep SAS records current.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCS leasing scope and band limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee may enter into spectrum manager or de facto transfer leasing or subleasing arrangements with a spectrum lessee only in the bands identified in § 2.106(d)(33)(i) for the purpose of meeting the part 25 SCS Entry Criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leasing for supplemental coverage from space is limited to specifically-identified bands and must be for meeting part 25 entry criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCS co-channel licensee leasing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a single licensee holds all co-channel licenses in a GIA, it may enter a leasing arrangement with one or more satellite operators. If multiple co-channel licensees jointly hold all co-channel licenses in a GIA, leasing is permitted only if either one terrestrial licensee leases with each other co-channel licensee and then leases to one satellite operator, or one satellite operator enters individual leases with each co-channel licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the leasing structure complies with single-licensee vs multiple-licensee alternatives and that GIA coverage is addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCS FCC Form 608 required certifications and demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum lessee seeking to engage in SCS leasing must provide on FCC Form 608: a certification that parties are entering the leasing to fulfill part 25 Entry Criteria; a description of the method (single or multiple terrestrial licensee) used; and, if using the multiple-terrestrial-licensee method, a description of the nature of the leasing arrangements and demonstration of how the entirety of the GIA is covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit certification and mapping/demonstration of coverage when multiple terrestrial licensees are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: FirstNet SCS filing requirements (FCC Form 601)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FirstNet to fulfill the part 25 SCS Entry Criteria, FirstNet must file an FCC Form 601 in ULS that: describes how FirstNet has conveyed authorization to its satellite partner to utilize specified bands; identifies/describes geographic areas and nature of proposed SCS operations; and demonstrates that rights/responsibilities of the satellite partner are substantively the same as those of a lessee under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FirstNet must use Form 601 and provide substantive evidence that partner rights mirror lessee obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCS subleasing restriction for multiple terrestrial licensee scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: Satellite operators may not enter into a spectrum subleasing arrangement where there are multiple terrestrial licensees jointly leasing their co-channel rights in a given GIA pursuant to the multiple-licensee scenario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subleasing by satellite operators is restricted in multiple-licensee joint-lease cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCS construction/performance attribution prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee may not attribute to itself the build-out or performance activities of its SCS spectrum lessee(s) for purposes of complying with any applicable performance or build-out requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees cannot take credit for lessee's activities to satisfy build-out/performance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private commons — definition and device-based access
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'private commons' is an arrangement where a licensee or spectrum lessee makes certain spectrum usage rights available to a class of third-party users employing advanced peer-to-peer (device-to-device) communications that do not involve use of the licensee's or lessee's end-to-end physical network infrastructure. It differs from spectrum leasing in that it does not involve individually negotiated spectrum access rights for entities seeking to provide network-based services to end-users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private commons are device-access models (peer-to-peer) and are distinct from network-based leasing; do not affect part 15 unlicensed operations permitted in the band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private commons — manager responsibilities to set technical/operating terms
rubrics_metrics.description: As manager of a private commons, the licensee or spectrum lessee establishes the technical and operating terms and conditions of use by users, including device types allowed, consistent with the underlying license authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers must define device/equipment rules and operational parameters in accordance with license conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private commons — de facto control and oversight obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee or spectrum lessee retains de facto control of the use of spectrum by users within the private commons and must maintain reasonable oversight to ensure use and equipment comply with all applicable technical and service rules (including RF radiation requirements) and must maintain the ability to ensure such compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain monitoring, enforcement, and the practical ability to intervene to ensure compliance by private-commons users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private commons — direct responsibility for compliance and interference
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee or spectrum lessee retains direct responsibility for ensuring that users of the private commons, and the equipment employed, comply with all applicable technical and service rules, including requirements relating to radiofrequency radiation and interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers remain liable for rules compliance and interference prevention; include compliance mechanisms and enforcement in operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private commons — FCC Form 608 notification content
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to permitting users to commence operations within a private commons, the licensee or spectrum lessee must notify the Commission using FCC Form 608, describing the location(s)/coverage area(s), the term of the arrangement, the general terms and conditions for users gaining access, the technical requirements and approved equipment, and the types of communications uses allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full description of the private commons parameters on Form 608 before user operations begin.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICFS purpose — electronic filing for International/Satellite services
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart describes procedures for electronic filing of International and Satellite Services applications using the International Communications Filing System (ICFS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ICFS for applicable international and satellite filings as required; see parts 1, 25, 63, 64 for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICFS official filing date rules (satellite vs others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Satellite Space Station applications (except DBS and DARS) and certain earth station applications are officially filed the moment they are filed through ICFS and a confirmation is received (date/time to the millisecond). For other applications, the official filing date is the date the application is filed and payment is received/approved, unless fee-exempt or otherwise specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness and queue ordering (e.g., § 25.158) may be based on filing timestamp; payment approval timing can affect official filing date for non-satellite forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICFS submission ID and matching payment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Submission ID is the confirmation number received from ICFS once you have successfully filed and is the number used to match your filing to your payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain Submission ID for payment reconciliation and proof of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing rule precedence when conflicts arise
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules concerning parts 1, 25, 63 and 64 govern over the electronic filing in this subpart when conflicts exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is a conflict between this subpart and parts 1/25/63/64, follow the specified parts' provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When operations may commence
rubrics_metrics.description: You can begin operating your facility or providing services once we grant your application to do so, under the conditions set forth in your license or authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not commence operations before grant and compliance with license conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to operate within license terms
rubrics_metrics.description: If approved and receive a license/authorization, you must operate in accordance with, and not beyond, your terms of approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure technical and service parameters conform to license limitations at all times.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICFS functions and record maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: ICFS is a database, application filing system, and processing system that supports electronic filing for the Space Bureau and Office of International Affairs and provides public access; ICFS maintains applications, notifications, correspondence, and other materials filed electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that ICFS is the repository and public access point for filings under these services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory electronic filing for forms available in ICFS
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic filing is mandatory for all applications for international and satellite services for which an ICFS form is available. Applications for which an electronic form is not available must be filed through ECFS in PDF until new forms are introduced. As each new ICFS form becomes available, manual filings for that form will not be accepted and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check ICFS for form availability and deadlines; manual submissions will be returned once electronic form is effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted attachment formats for ICFS
rubrics_metrics.description: Many applications require exhibits or attachments which must be attached to the electronic application before filing. Accepted formats: Word, Adobe Acrobat, Excel, and Text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare exhibits in accepted formats and attach them prior to filing; failure to attach required exhibits may cause rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICFS file numbers are administrative only
rubrics_metrics.description: ICFS assigns file numbers to electronic applications for processing convenience; they do not mean that an application is acceptable for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interpret assignment of a file number as determination of acceptability—substantive review still applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 — FRN registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants, transferees/assignees, transferors/assignors, licensees/authorization holders, or payers are required to have and use an FCC Registration Number (FRN) when filing applications and/or paying fees through ICFS. The FRN is used to give secured access and to pre-fill the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain an FRN from CORES or via ICFS before filing; include correct FRNs for applicant and payer on payment forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 — ICFS account registration
rubrics_metrics.description: To file electronically you must register with ICFS (at https://www.fcc.gov/icfs) and will be issued an account number and create a password; registration may be in your name, your company's, or your client's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep account credentials secure; ICFS helpline available for password assistance (icfsinfo@fcc.gov, (202) 418-2222).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 — Complete all required information and provide contact/address
rubrics_metrics.description: Log into ICFS, select application, provide required FRN(s) and passwords and fill out application completely per parts 1, 25, 63, 64. Provide a USPS mail-deliverable address and encouraged to provide email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all form data is completed; include mailing address for communications and potential requests for additional documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 — Incorporation by reference allowed with conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may incorporate previously-filed documents by reference if the referenced information is filed in ICFS, is current and accurate, and the application states where we can find the referenced information (application file number, title/docket/legal citation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise cross-references and ensure referenced documents are up-to-date and in ICFS to be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 4 — Confirmation and proof of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you file successfully through ICFS, a confirmation screen will show date/time of filing and submission ID; print verification as proof of online filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain confirmation screen and Submission ID for your records; this serves as proof of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 5 — Payment procedures and fee determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Most applications require payment before processing. Determine fee via § 1.1107, the International and Satellite Services fee guide, or by running a draft electronic submission in ICFS. A complete FCC electronic submission of payment online form must accompany all fee payments and must provide the FRN for applicant and payer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure payment method (ACH, credit card, wire transfer) is supported and payment is properly documented with FRNs; payment approval may determine official filing date for non-satellite filings.
